Creed Rowland Bratton (claims to have been born November 1, 1925) is a fictional character from the U.S. television series The Office. The character is played by the musician of the same name, Creed Bratton. The fictional Creed is partially based on the experiences and former flower child lifestyle of the real one. Series writer B. J. Novak has said that the actual Creed Bratton is exactly like the character he plays, except that the real Creed is a good-hearted and likable person.

Cree Elizabeth Cicchino (born 9 May 2002) is an American actor. She began her career as a child actor playing one of the lead roles, Babe Carano, on the Nickelodeon comedy television show Game Shakers. She then went on to play Marisol Fuentes on the Netflix comedy television show Mr. Iglesias, and to play Mim in the 2020 Netflix movie The Sleepover.

Creed Taylor (May 13, 1929 – August 23, 2022) was an American record producer. He was best known for his work with CTI Records, which he founded in 1967. He also worked for Bethlehem Records, ABC-Paramount Records (including its jazz label, Impulse!), Verve, and A&M Records. Taylor died on August 23, 2022, at the age of 93.

Cricket Leigh is an American actress. Cricket was born in Michigan, raised in Chicago and graduated from New York University before moving to Los Angeles. She played all eight characters in, and wrote Constantly Distracted in 2005. She also played Alma on Pop Tarts in 1999. In 2002, Cricket Leigh voiced Tangier in Red Faction 2. In 2003, she played Mala in Terra. She played Bernice on Boys & Girls Guide To Getting Down in 2006. She began voicing Mai in Avatar: The Last Airbender in seasons 2 and 3. As of 2007, she provided the voice of Basil in Capcom's 3rd-person action game Lost Planet: Extreme Condition.

Criss Angel (born Christopher Nicholas Sarantakos, December 19, 1967) is an American illusionist, stuntperformer, and musician. He has done many illusions. Examples of these include walking on water, making an Asian elephant vanish and then reappear several episodes later, and floating between two buildings. Angel has had a television program on the American network A&E called Criss Angel Mindfreak. The program has stunts and street magic, as well as public service announcements about scams that are popular around the United States. Angel was the guest host of the March 8, 2010 version of WWE Monday Night Raw.

Crispin Hellion Glover (born April 20, 1964) is an American actor. He has acted in such movies as Back to the Future, Epic Movie (where he did a parody of the Willy Wonka played by Johnny Depp) and the Open Season series as Fifi. In the late 1980s, Glover started his company, Volcanic Eruptions. The company publishes his books and also is the production company for his movies, What Is It? and It is Fine. Everything is Fine!. Glover has written between 15 and 20 books. He makes the books by reusing old novels and other publications which are in the public domain due to their age. He rearranges text, blacks out certain standing passages, and adds his own prose and sometimes images. His father is actor Bruce Glover. His mother was Betty Glover who died in 2016.

Christopher Michael Oliva (April 3, 1963 – October 17, 1993) was an American musician. He was one of the creators of the heavy metal band Savatage. He was the lead guitarist for the band as well. He made seven albums with the band. In 1993, Oliva died when a drunk driver hit the car he was in. In 2025, Savatage returned and honored Criss by keeping his music alive, and payed video tribute during the song "Believe," sung in part by his brother Jon.

Cris Williamson (born February 15, 1947) is an American feminist singer-songwriter and political activist. She is known as a lesbian rights activist. She is seen as an important activist in the LGBTQ+ community. Williamson was born in Deadwood, South Dakota. She was raised in Colorado and Wyoming.

Cristina Deutekom, also known as Christine Deutekom and Christina Deutekom (28 August 1931 – 7 August 2014) was a Dutch coloratura soprano opera singer. Deutekom's stage career ended in 1986, when she suffered a heart attack. She sang with all the leading tenors of her time, including Carlo Bergonzi, José Carreras, Franco Corelli, Plácido Domingo, Nicolai Gedda, Alfredo Kraus, Luciano Pavarotti, and Richard Tucker. Deutekom was born in 1931 in Amsterdam as Christine (Stientje) Engel. Her career began in 1963. She died on 7 August 2014 after a fall in her home.

Cristiano Melo Araújo (January 24, 1986 – June 24, 2015) was a Brazilian singer and songwriter. Araújo was famous for the singles "Efeitos" (2011), "Você mudou" (2012), "Maus bocados"(2013), "Cê que sabe" (2014) and "É com ela que eu estou" (2014) Araújo and his girlfriend, Allana Moares, 19, died early on 24 June 2015 in a car accident on the BR-153 at km 614, between Morrinhos and Pontalina in Goiás.

Cristin Milioti (born August 16, 1985) is an American actress and singer. She is best known for playing the Mother on the sitcom How I Met Your Mother from 2013 to 2014 and Sofia Falcone in the 2024 DC Comics limited television series The Penguin. She has also played Teresa Petrillo in the 2013 movie The Wolf of Wall Street, and Betsy Solverson in the second season of Fargo (2015).

Cristina Monet-Palaci (January 17, 1956 – March 31, 2020), better known as Cristina, was an American singer. She is best known for her new wave recordings made for Ze Records around the early 1980s in New York City. Her two studio albums were reissued in 2004. Notable singles by Cristina include "Disco Clone", "Is That All There Is?", "Drive My Car" and "Things Fall Apart". On March 31, 2020, during the 2019–20 coronavirus pandemic, Cristina died of COVID-19. She was 64.

Christian Sáinz Valdés Castro (born 8 December 1974), known professionally as Cristian Castro or Cristian, is a Mexican pop singer. He is the son of actors Veronica Castro and Manuel "El Loco" Valdés. He is known for his slight tenor vocal singing. Castro is known as one of the most well known Hispanic pop singers of the last three decades. Juan Gabriel described Castro as "the man with the most faculties to sing in Mexico".

Cristian Taraborrelli was born in Rome and started working in theater in the early 1990s. He is a talented opera and show director, set designer and costume designer known for his work in both experimental theater and opera. In the early 1990s, he worked with Giorgio Barberio Corsetti and Fabio Massimo Iaquone on experimental theater projects. Taraborrelli began to gain recognition for his own work in 2006, when he started directing performances himself. That same year, he won the Franco Abbiati Prize from Italian music critics. In 2009, he received the Prix du Syndicat de la Critique for best set design for the play "Gertrude - The Cry." Taraborrelli's style is unique and innovative. He likes to explore the balance and changes in theater, using techniques like suspensions, reversals, and deformations. His set designs often have an abstract feel, using unusual materials and modern technology to create engaging and thought-provoking scenes. His costumes blend tradition with modern styles, helping to express the characters' personalities and emotions. Beyond theater, Taraborrelli's creativity extends to other spaces, such as his work on the setup of the Aquarium of Genoa and various installations. Cynthia Cristina Ferrare (born 1950) is an American fashion model, actress, author and talk-show host. She is known for her roles in the 1968 comedy The Impossible Years and the 1972 Western movie J. W. Coop. She also played the lead role in the horror movie Mary, Mary, Bloody Mary (1972). She also hosted The Home Show, Home & Family, and Big Bowl of Love on the Oprah Winfrey Network in the 1980s.

Cristián de la Fuente Sabarots (born 10 March 1974) is a Chilean actor. He studied mechanical engineering in Puerto Rico. He loves sports very much. At first, he was a model.He started acting in small roles in television series and movies. Internationally, he became famous with the movie Driven, from 2001. Today, de la Fuente Sabarots lives in Los Angeles. He is married, and has a daughter.

Cristina Stamate (8 September 1946 – 27 November 2017) was a Romanian actress. She was born in Bucharest. She was best known for her stage performances. She spent most of her career at the Teatrul de Revistă Constantin Tănase in Bucharest. She appeared in two movies, Grăbește-te încet (1981) and Secretul lui Bachus (1984). Stamate died on 27 November 2017 in Bucharest after having a stroke. She was 71. On the day of her death, she learned of the death of her friend, actress Stela Popescu.

Cristóbal Halffter Jiménez-Encina (24 March 1930 – 23 May 2021) was a Spanish classical composer and conductor. He was the nephew of two other composers, Rodolfo and Ernesto Halffter. He was seen as the most important Spanish composer of the generation of composers during the Generación del 51. He was born in Madrid. During the 1960s and 1970s, Halffter composed a number of works relating to human rights, including the 1968 choral work Yes, speak out, yes. He was awarded Spain's highest award for composition, the Premio Nacional de Música, in 1989. Halffter died on 23 May 2021 in Villafranca del Bierzo, Spain at the age of 91.

Cristina Danielle Valenzuela (born July 11, 1987), known professionally as Cristina Vee, is an American voice actress and singer. She is best known for her work in English-language dubs of anime and in video games. Cristina Vee was born Cristina Danielle Valenzuela in Los Angeles, California, on July 11, 1987. She has Lebanese, Indigenous Mexican (Tepehuán), and Spanish ancestry. Vee grew up in Norwalk, California, where she attended public school. She became interested in music at an early age and participated in the Norwalk All City band during middle school and high school. Her classmates called her "Sailor Moon Girl" because of her interest in acting and animation. She also helped start the anime club at John Glenn High School. Vee studied theatre arts at California State University, Long Beach, graduating in 2007. During college, Vee experienced depression and panic attacks that made it difficult for her to attend classes. She later explained that, although she enjoyed studying theatre and performing in productions, college was a difficult period in her life. Vee originally wanted to become an animator. However, after watching Sailor Moon at the age of 12, she became interested in voice acting. By the age of 16, she had already spent four years doing voice work for amateur online projects. She attended Anime Expo as a fan several times and took part in its AX Idol voice-over contest. In 2004, Vee participated in a voice-over panel at Anime Expo. She helped operate some of the equipment and received a card from voice actress Wendee Lee, who encouraged her to audition for projects at Bang Zoom! Entertainment. One of her early projects was the anime Samurai Champloo. Her first major role was Kanaria in Rozen Maiden. In 2008, Vee voiced the main character in Aika R-16: Virgin Mission, Louise in The Familiar of Zero, and Nanoha in Magical Girl Lyrical Nanoha. She also portrayed Haruhi Suzumiya in promotional videos for the second The Melancholy of Haruhi Suzumiya series and appeared as the character at public events. In 2011, Vee voiced Mio Akiyama in the music comedy series K-On! and Nagisa Saitō in Squid Girl. She also voiced Alisa Bosconovitch in the animated film Tekken: Blood Vengeance and attended anime conventions with the film's writer, Dai Satō, to promote it. In 2012, she voiced Homura Akemi in Puella Magi Madoka Magica. In 2013, she voiced Princess Yo in Nura: Rise of the Yokai Clan and Red Hood in the Ikki Tousen series. The following year, she voiced Morgiana in Magi: The Labyrinth of Magic and the Honoka sisters in Knights of Sidonia. In 2014, Vee was chosen to voice Sailor Mars, also known as Rei Hino, in the new English dub of Sailor Moon and the series Sailor Moon Crystal. She explained that her portrayal in Crystal was different because Rei was more serious and formal in that series. In 2015, Vee voiced Noel Vermillion in BlazBlue Alter Memory, Compa in Hyperdimension Neptunia: The Animation, and Hawk in The Seven Deadly Sins. In 2016, she voiced Killua Zoldyck in the English dub of the 2011 anime adaptation of Hunter × Hunter. In 2021, Vee voiced Vivy in the English dub of the original anime series Vivy: Fluorite Eye's Song. In 2025, she voiced Stocking in a new English dub of Panty & Stocking with Garterbelt, replacing Monica Rial, who had voiced the character in the earlier dub. In 2012, Vee started a Kickstarter campaign to fund an animated music video with Cybergraphix Animation and Studio APPP. The video's main character, originally called Cristina Veecaloid, was designed by Skullgirls creative director Alex Ahad. The character was later named Milky and became the basis for the mobile game Veecaloid Pop, which was released in 2015. In 2012, Vee worked on voice casting and voice direction for the video game Skullgirls and its web series. The game was nominated for an Annie Award. In 2015, Vee began voicing Marinette Dupain-Cheng, also known as Ladybug, in the English dub of the animated series Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir. The series premiered on Nickelodeon in December 2015. Vee's performance has been praised by the show's executive producer, Jared Wolfsen, who described her as similar to Ladybug in personality. Vee also voices Verosika Mayday in the animated web series Helluva Boss. She appeared as the character in episodes released in 2021 and 2024, including "Spring Broken", "Ozzie's", and "Apology Tour". In June 2023, it was announced that Vee would voice Tere and Toñita in the animated series Primos. The series premiered on Disney Channel in July 2024. Vee has voiced characters in many video games, including English-language versions of Japanese games. Some of her roles include Noel Vermillion in BlazBlue, Velvet Crowe in Tales of Berseria, Riven in League of Legends, Four in Drakengard 3, Compa in Hyperdimension Neptunia, Ying in Paladins: Champions of the Realm, and 13-Amp and 5-Volt in the WarioWare series. Her other roles include Marnie in Pokémon Masters EX, Tulin in The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, the title character in the Shantae series, Bennett and Xingqiu in Genshin Impact, the Dahlia in Honkai: Star Rail, and Hoshimi Miyabi in Zenless Zone Zero. She also voiced Risky Boots, the main character Shantae's enemy, in the Shantae series. Vee has also worked as a voice director and producer. She directed and produced the voice work for the video game Indivisible, which raised $1.5 million through crowdfunding in 2015. Vee has also hosted and appeared in online shows, television programs, and live events. She hosted Anime TV, where she reviewed anime and interviewed guests, and appeared on programs for Funimation and Crunchyroll. She also hosted the League of Legends tournaments IPL4 and IPL5 for IGN in Las Vegas. She has also appeared as a guest at anime conventions in the United States and other countries. Vee is also a singer. She performed "Dance Through the Danger" for the 2016 video game Shantae: Half-Genie Hero and "Rise and Shine Shantae" for the 2019 game Shantae and the Seven Sirens. She also performed "Until I'm Broken" for the 2012 visual novel Loren the Amazon Princess. Vee has performed several songs for the mobile game Arknights, including "Boiling Blood", "ALIVE", "Spark for Dream", and "Water Quench". In 2023, she performed the ending theme for the English dub of Digimon Adventure:, titled "KUYASHISAWA TANE". She has also uploaded covers of anime songs to YouTube. In 2015, she released an extended play (EP) titled Menagerie with DJ Bouche through Viewster's Omakase subscription service. In August 2017, she and YouTuber Nathan Sharp, also known as NateWantsToBattle, released a cover of Charlie Puth's song "Attention". She later signed with the independent record label Give Heart Records. Vee has also recorded a cover of "Animal" by The Living Tombstone with the 8-Bit Big Band, arranged by Charlie Rosen. In April 2024, she released a cover of "Whatever It Takes" from the animated series Hazbin Hotel, featuring Sofia Gomez and Tre Watson. Vee moved from Norwalk to the Eagle Rock area of Los Angeles in 2012. In January 2018, Vee became engaged to voice actor and musician Nathan Sharp. The couple separated in August 2018. In February 2024, an anonymous user on Twitter incorrectly included Vee on a list of voice actors accused of being Zionists. Vee and her fans responded by sharing evidence of her support for Palestine and participation in boycotts opposing Zionism. She received death threats and later deactivated her account. The user who posted the list apologized and later deactivated their account following criticism.

Cristina Scuccia (born 19 August 1988) is an Italian singer. She won the 2014 season of The Voice of Italy as part of Team J-Ax, resulting in a record deal with Universal. In 2013, she won a Christian music competition as part of the Good News Festival.

Crunchy Black (born August 1974 in Indiana) is an American rapper and dancer from Memphis, Tennessee. He is one of the original six members of the Oscar-winning hip hop group Three 6 Mafia though he would leave the group in 2006. Crunchy is known for his dancing "G-Walking", which he says he started doing at Club Memphis. He is not the starter of this dance but he is very good at it. He is known as a pioneer. Crunchy Black is highly respected in the hip-hop community. He is a pioneer of Memphis rap.

"Crush with Eyeliner" is a 1995 song by American alternative rock band R.E.M. and is the fourth single from their ninth studio album Monster (1994). It went to number 4 in Iceland, number 21 in Ireland, number 23 in the United Kingdom, number 28 in Canada, number 45 in Belgium and number 55 in Australia. It did not chart in the United States.

Crystal Kay Williams (born 26 February 1986 in Yokohama, Japan) is a Japanese-born singer, songwriter, actress and radio host. She is also known as "Kuri" by her fans. She is well known for her songs "Koi ni Ochitara" and "Boyfriend -part II-". As of April 2021, she has released thirteen albums. Born and raised in Yokohama to an African-American father and a Japanese mother of Korean descent, Crystal Kay speaks English and Japanese fluently and records music in both languages. In 2003 she released an English compilation album called Natural: World Premiere Album. She started singing on television commercials when she was four years old. When she was twelve she was signed to Epic Records. Kay's first album C.L.L Crystal Lover Light was released on March 23, 2000 when Kay was fourteen. 2006: Call me Miss... 2008: Color Change!
Crystal Bernard (born September 30, 1961) is an American sitcom actress. She also does other television acting. She is best known for her role in the NBC sitcom Wings.

Crystal Lowe (born January 20, 1981) is a Canadian actress and model. She is best known for her roles in horror movies such as roles as Children of the Corn: Revelation (2001), Final Destination 3 (2006), Black Christmas (2006) and Wrong Turn 2: Dead End (2007). In February 2025, Lowe was diagnosed with stage-3 breast cancer.

Crystal Marie Reed (born February 6, 1985) is an American actress, best known for playing Allison Argent on the Teen Wolf television series. Reed played Sofia Falcone in the fourth season of Gotham (2017–2018) and the lead role of Abby Arcane in the series Swamp Thing (2019).

Crystal (born May 6, 1994) is a female capuchin monkey and animal actress. She starred in the Disney's 1997 movie George of the Jungle. She also played the annoying monkey Dexter in the Night at the Museum and a drug-dealing monkey in The Hangover Part II.

Crystal Waters (born November 19, 1961) is an American house and dance music singer-songwriter. She is best known for her hits, "Gypsy Woman", "100% Pure Love" and "Destination Calabria" with Alex Gaudino. All three of her studio albums produced a Top 40 hit on the Billboard Hot 100. In December 2016, Billboard magazine ranked her as one of the most successful dance artists of all time. She has sold 7 million records worldwide.

Csaba Kőrösi is a Hungarian politician. He was the Director of Environmental Sustainability in the Office of the President of Hungary. In June 2022 was elected to be the President of the United Nations General Assembly for its seventy-seventh session.

Cuba Mark Gooding (April 27, 1944 – April 20, 2017) was the lead singer of the soul group The Main Ingredient and actor. This group is most notable for the songs "Everybody Plays the Fool" (1972) and "Just Don't Want to Be Lonely" (1974). Gooding also had a brief solo career on Motown Records during the late 1970s and early 1980s. His most successful song internationally was "Happiness Is Just Around the Bend" in 1983. In recent times this song been sampled by several R&B artists, as well as hitting the charts again as a remix by UK Hardcore Rave pranksters/genii Altern-8 in 1991. Gooding was born in New York City. He has four children, including actors Cuba Gooding, Jr. (born 1968) and Omar Gooding (born 1976). Gooding was found dead in his car on the afternoon of April 20, 2017 in Woodland Hills, California, aged 72. Police believe he died from a suspected drug overdose.

Cuba Gooding, Jr. (born January 2, 1968) is an American actor who was born in New York City. He won an Academy Award for his performance in Jerry Maguire. In 2016, he portrayed O.J. Simpson in the FX drama series The People v. O. J. Simpson: American Crime Story, and co-starred in the sixth season of the FX anthology series American Horror Story, subtitled Roanoke. His father is singer Cuba Gooding, Sr. The family moved to Los Angeles in 1972. Gooding has been a born-again Christian since he was 13.

Cung Lê or Lê Cung (born May 25, 1972) is a Vietnamese-born American actor and former kickboxer and Mixed Martial Arts professional. He invincible on the Sanshou Kickboxing arena with a 17-0 record, the International Kickboxing Federation Championship Light Heavyweight Championship before moving to Mixed Martial Arts. Cung Lê defeated Frank Shamrock and became the middleweight champion of Strikeforce before resigning to pursue a film career and joining the UFC, the world's largest free-spirited tournament.

Elizabeth Eden Harris, known more professionally as Cupcakke (also stylized as CupcakKe), is an American rapper. Cupcakke was born in Chicago, Illinois. She is known for her explicit songs She is known for her songs like CPR, Deepthroat, and more rap songs. These songs went viral on the video platform YouTube. Later, she became more popular because of different versions of her songs. These versions were made by fans, which are called remixed songs. These became popular on social media app TikTok. Curd Gustav Andreas Gottlieb Franz Jürgens (13 December 191518 June 1982) was a German-Austrian actor. He played Ernst Udet in Des Teufels General. He also played James Bond villain Karl Stromberg in The Spy Who Loved Me (1977).

Jerome Lester Horwitz (October 22, 1903 – January 18, 1952), known professionally as Curly Howard, was an American comedian and actor. Howard joined the group of Ted Healy and his Stooges, in 1932 replacing his brother Shemp. He had to shave his moustache and shave his hair to join the group. The first film shot with Ted Healy and His Stooges was Nertsery Rhymes (1933), followed by Beer and Pretzels (1933), directed by Jack Cummings. In 1934, the Stooges separated from Ted Healy, and started working as The Three Stooges. Curly Howard, Larry Fine and Moe Howard filmed together 97 short films, between 1932 and 1947. He made appearances with Moe and Larry in such films as Fugitive Lovers (1934) and Time Out for Rhythm (1941).

Sir Currimbhoy Ebrahim (or Currimbhoy Ebrahim), 3rd Baronet, JP (born 1903- died 1952), was a prominent businessman, philanthropist and political leader from Bombay, British India. He succeeded his father Sir Mohamedbhoy Ebrahim as Baronet, and as managing director of many family-owned firms. He also became director or chairman of many charitable trusts in the Bombay area and in 1936, started the Muslim Peace and Relief Committee. In the same year, he became a member of the All India Muslim League and an active political leader of this party.

Shante Scott Franklin (born April 4, 1981), better known by his stage name Currensy (stylized as Curren$y) is an American rapper, songwriter and record executive. Formerly signed to Lil Wayne's record label Young Money Entertainment, he signed himself to No Limit Records as a teenager. After releasing mixtapes, his first album This Ain't No Mixtape was released in April 2009. After gaining stream in 2007, he made a shocking move leaving Young Money to do his own thing on an airplane. Currensy said, "I ain't see nothing coming out of there. I have been on Young Money for like 4 years. We had the "Where The Cash At" video game, you know, that was cool".

Curry Barker (born September 22, 1999) is an American filmmaker, actor, comedian, and YouTuber. He is known for the sketch comedy YouTube channel "that's a bad idea". He directed and wrote the horror movies Milk & Serial (2024) and Obsession (2025). In April 2026, it was announced that Barker would be writing and directing a reboot of The Texas Chain Saw Massacre with A24. Barker was born on September 22, 1999 in Mobile, Alabama.

Curt Lowens (17 November 1925 – 8 May 2017) was an American actor of the stage and in feature movies and television, as well as a Holocaust survivor and a rescuer who saved about 150 Jewish children during the Holocaust. He was known for his roles as Director Swift in Werewolf in a Girls' Dormitory (1962) and as a Soviet ambassador on The A-Team, appearing from 1983 through 1987. He was also in Angels & Demons. Lowens died in 8 May 2017 in New York City at the age of 91.

Curtis Armstrong (born November 27, 1953) is an American actor best known for playing the roles of Booger in the Revenge of the Nerds movies, Herbert Viola on the TV series Moonlighting, Miles Dalby in the film Risky Business, famed record producer Ahmet Ertegün in the film Ray as well as for playing the role of Metatron on the TV series Supernatural. He is also known for providing his voice for such characters as Schmuley "Snot" Lonstein on the animated TV series American Dad! and Maru in the animated film Planes: Fire & Rescue in addition to portraying the title character on the animated TV series Dan Vs. From 2013 to 2015, he served as the co-host of the TBS reality television competition series King of the Nerds and the bank manager in neo-western crime film Hell or High Water.

Curtis L. McClarin (December 3, 1969 – March 3, 2014) was an American actor. He had roles in movies, television shows and musical theater plays. He appeared in the movies The Hard Way (1991), Fresh (1994) and The Happening (2008), the television movie Murder Without Motive: The Edmund Perry Story about the death of Edmund Perry, and on Broadway in the Tony Award-nominated musical Bring in 'da Noise, Bring in 'da Funk. He was born in the borough of Brooklyn, New York City, New York. McClarin died in his sleep from a brain aneurysm on March 3, 2014 in his hometown of Brooklyn. He was 44 years old.

Curtis Lee Mayfield (June 3, 1942 – December 26, 1999) was an American guitarist, singer-songwriter and record producer. He was one of the most influential musicians behind soul and the politically conscious African-American music. He first achieved success and recognition with the R&B and soul group The Impressions during the civil rights movement in the 1950s and 1960s. The Impressions were later put into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. Mayfield later decided to work on his own. Mayfield began his music career in a gospel choir. He got involved with The Impressions shortly after moving to the North Side of Chicago. In 1965, Mayfield wrote the song "People Get Ready" for The Impressions. The song was later ranked at #24 on the Rolling Stone list for 500 Greatest Songs of All Time. The song got several other awards. It was included into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame's 500 Songs That Shaped Rock and Roll. "People Get Ready" was added into the Grammy Hall of Fame in 1998. Mayfield left The Impressions in 1970 in the pursuit of working on his own. He released several studio albums, including the soundtrack for the blaxploitation movie, Super Fly in 1972. The soundtrack dealt with crimes involving inner-city minorities, like substance abuse, poverty and crime. Mayfield was paralyzed from the neck down when lighting equipment fell on him while he was performing live at the Wingate Field in the Flatbush neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York. However, he continued his career as a recording artist. His last studio album was New World Order in 1996. Mayfield won the Grammy Legend Award in 1994 and the Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award one year later. Mayfield was born in the Cook County hospital in Chicago, Illinois. He died in Roswell, Georgia from type 2 diabetes complications at age 57 the day after Christmas 1999.

Cuthbert Augustus "Bill" Pattillo (June 3, 1924 – February 20, 2014) was a Major General in the United States Air Force. He served in World War II and the Vietnam War. He worked as Director of Plans and Policy for the United States Readiness Command at MacDill Air Force Base. He was as a pioneer in jet aerobatic demonstration teams. He was born in Atlanta, Georgia. His twin brother was Charles C. Pattillo. Pattillo died from natural causes on February 20, 2014 at his home in Harrisonburg, Virginia. He was 89 years old.

Cya Liu (born 13 January 1989) is a Chinese singer and actress. Her birth name is Liu Xin. She was a member of the girl group OP. She became popular after acting in the movie So Young in 2013. In 2022, she won the Best Actress award at the Hong Kong Film Awards for her role in the movie Limbo.

Cybill Lynne Shepherd (born February 18, 1950) is an American actress. She has acted in many sitcoms, television programs and movies. She starred in Moonlighting with Bruce Willis. Shepherd had melanoma in 2002.

Cyd Charisse (March 8, 1922 – June 17, 2008) was an American actress and dancer. She was known for her roles in Singin' in the Rain (1952), The Band Wagon (1953) and Silk Stockings (1957). Charisse was born in Amarillo, Texas. She was married to Tony Martin. Charisse died in Los Angeles, California from a heart attack, aged 87.

Cynthia Ann Stephanie "Cyndi" Lauper (born June 22, 1953) is an American Grammy Award-winning singer, songwriter, and MTV VMA-winning video and Emmy Award-winning movie, television, and theater actress. She became very well known in the mid-1980s with the release of the album, She's So Unusual. Lauper became the first artist in history to have four top-five singles released from one album. She has released 11 albums, over 40 singles, and has sold more than 60 million albums worldwide. She continues to tour the world in support of human rights. Merry Christmas... Have a Nice Life (1998) The Grammy Awards are awarded annually by the National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences. Lauper has won one award from 15 nominations.

Cynthia Lee Harris (August 9, 1934 – October 3, 2021) was an American actress. She was best known for her roles in the television series Edward & Mrs. Simpson and the sitcom Mad About You. She also appeared in the 1987 comedy movie Three Men and a Baby. Harris was born in New York City. Harris died on October 3, 2021 in New York City, aged 87.

Cynthia Chinasaokwu Onyedinmanasu Amarachukwu Owezuke Echimino Erivo, known by just Cynthia Erivo (; born 8 January 1987) is an English actress and singer-songwriter. She has won a Daytime Emmy Award, a Grammy Award, and a Tony Award. She was in the Broadway revival of The Color Purple from 2015 to 2017. She played Harriet Tubman in the biopic Harriet (2019), for which she received a nomination for the Academy Award for Best Actress. She starred as Elphaba in the 2024 musical fantasy movie Wicked. She is a vegan.

Cynthia Corla Pricillia, known as Bunda Corla (born July 4, 1974) is an Indonesian internet celebrity, singer, and actress. She is best known for her status as a viral internet personality and her music career. AMI Awards for Best Male/Female Electro Dangdut Solo Artist/Group/Collaboration.

Cynthia Lowrie Gibb (born December 14, 1963) is an American actress and former model. Her first acting role was in the musical television drama Fame, based on the movie of the same name. Gibb also appeared in the movies Youngblood (1986), Salvador (1986), Malone (1987), Short Circuit 2 (1988) and Death Warrant (1990). She earned a Golden Globe nomination for her role as Gypsy Rose Lee in the movie Gypsy (1993). Cynthia Lowrie Gibb was born December 14, 1963, in Bennington, Vermont. She grew up in Westport, Connecticut.

Cynthia Ellen Nixon (born April 9, 1966) is an American actress, activist and politician. She is most well known role comes from playing Miranda Hobbes in the HBO series Sex and the City (1998-2004). She has had other movie and TV starring acts as well. In 2016, she played Nancy Reagan in the television movie Killing Reagan. On March 19, 2018, she announced via Twitter that she was running for Governor of New York.

Cynthia Jeanette Myers (September 12, 1950 – November 4, 2011) was an American actress and fashion model. She acted primarily in B-movies. She was Playboy Playmate of the Month in December 1968. Her most famous theatrical movie was Beyond the Valley of the Dolls, a 1970 movie in which she starred as bisexual musician Casey Anderson. Myers was born in Toledo, Ohio.
